methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece identifies small-business AI adoption as Virginia's core challenge rather than infrastructure—signaling that shallow engagement persists even as data centers concentrate capital, pointing toward neither depth nor distribution materializing at scale.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: UVA students consulting with businesses on AI exploration represents peer-to-peer knowledge transfer and hands-on capability building—a distributed model that could spread deep fluency through community networks rather than platform dependency.

signals.title: Why this Virginia Tech professor says don't use AI for medical advice - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech professor providing expert AI medical advice guidance demonstrates concentrated research expertise in the New River Valley hub, but commentary format suggests knowledge remains siloed rather than translating into broad regional capability.

signals.title: Norfolk looks to add AI dispatcher tool for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk adopting AI dispatcher for non-emergency calls shows platform-delivered automation enabling municipal capability without deep technical expertise—exemplifying shallow but functional distributed adoption through vendor solutions.

signals.title: Virginia authorizes funding for VCU to purchase Altria Center for Research and Technology - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: State funding for VCU to acquire research and technology center reinforces capital region's institutional AI capacity, concentrating resources in metro areas while creating potential but unproven conduits for knowledge distribution to surrounding regions.
